   MCP: after a simulator is erased and rebooted, every run fails with "Device became unreachable during setPermissions" until maestro mcp restarts (repro for #3368)   #3700 New issue Copy link New issue Copy link Open Open MCP: after a simulator is erased and rebooted, every run fails with "Device became unreachable during setPermissions" until maestro mcp restarts (repro for #3368) #3700 Copy link Description michael-mcclintock opened  on Oct 20, 2026 Issue body actions Is there an existing issue for this? 
 
  I have searched the existing issues and didn't find mine. This is a deterministic reproduction of  iOS: XCUITest driver becomes unreachable mid-suite and is never restarted — every later flow fails at setPermissions (Failed to connect to /127.0.0.1:<port>)  #3368  ("XCUITest driver becomes unreachable mid-suite and is never restarted — every later flow fails at setPermissions"), which was closed for lack of a reproduction and is now locked. 
 
 Steps to reproduce 
 
 Boot an iOS Simulator ( xcrun simctl boot <udid> ) and install any app. 
 Start  one  long-lived  maestro mcp --no-viewer  process and use it against that simulator. A  run  with a flow that starts with  launchApp  succeeds. 
 Without restarting  maestro mcp , reset the same simulator in place:
 xcrun simctl shutdown  < udid > 
xcrun simctl erase  < udid > 
xcrun simctl boot  < udid > 
xcrun simctl install  < udid >   < app > .app 
 
 Call the MCP  run  tool again with the same flow file (it starts with  launchApp ). 
 Call it again. 
 
 Actual results 
 Steps 4 and 5 both fail immediately, before any command runs: 
 { "success" : false , "total_commands_executed" : 0 , "results" :[{ "success" : false , "error" : " Device became unreachable during setPermissions " , "message" : " Flow execution failed " }]} 
 Retrying never recovers. Restarting  maestro mcp  fixes it: a fresh process runs the same flow successfully on the same simulator. 
 Expected results 
 The MCP server notices that its driver session for that device is gone (the simulator was erased and rebooted, which removes the on-device XCUITest runner) and re-establishes it on the next call, as a fresh process does. 
 About app 
 Reproduced with an Expo development build. The failure happens in  launchApp 's  setPermissions , before any app-specific command. 
 About environment 
 macOS 26.5.2, Xcode 26.6, iOS Simulator runtime iOS 26.5 (iPhone 17). 
 Logs 
 Device became unreachable during setPermissions
 
 (Same symptom as  #3368 : the driver connection is never rotated after the device side goes away.) 
 Maestro version 
 2.7.0 
 How did you install Maestro? 
 curl | bash 
 Anything else? 
 Erasing and rebooting a simulator between sessions is a normal pattern for anything that hands clean simulators to agents or CI jobs, which is how we hit it. Our workaround is one  maestro mcp  process per session, closed before the simulator is erased.
